Set up the integral for the volume of revolution between the line $y = 5 - x$ and the curve $y = \frac{4}{x}$ rotated about the $x$-axis from $x = 1$ to $x = 4$:
$$V = \pi \int_1^4 \left(y_{\text{line}}^2 - y_{\text{curve}}^2\right) dx = \pi \int_1^4 \left[(5 - x)^2 - \left(\frac{4}{x}\right)^2\right] dx$$

Expand and integrate term by term:
$$V = \pi \int_1^4 \left(25 - 10x + x^2 - 16x^{-2}\right) dx = \pi \left[ 25x - 5x^2 + \frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{16}{x} \right]_1^4$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 1$ and subtract:
$$F(1) = 25(1) - 5(1^2) + \frac{1^3}{3} + \frac{16}{1} = 25 - 5 + \frac{1}{3} + 16 = 36 + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{109}{3}$$
$$V = \pi \left( \frac{136}{3} - \frac{109}{3} \right) = \pi \left(\frac{27}{3}\right) = 9\pi \quad (\approx 28.3\text{ units}^3)$$
